additions.definition: A holder that supports a coffee filter and grounds while poured water drains through them into a vessel below. Its shape and openings influence the flow; the dripper is distinct from the filter it holds.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A coffee brewer with a vessel and plunger-mounted filter. Grounds steep in the water before the filter is lowered to retain them for pouring. This immersion arrangement differs from water passing through a separate pour-over dripper.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A tool that reduces roasted coffee beans to particles for brewing. Grind adjustment and mechanism vary; a grinder prepares grounds but does not brew the drink. The documented burr grinder is one example, not a definition of every coffee grinder.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A machine that extracts coffee by passing pressurised hot water through prepared grounds. A steam wand, when fitted, performs a separate milk-texturing task. A built-in grinder or automatic milk system is not implied by the name.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A handled jug used to hold milk during texturing and pour it into a drink. A shaped spout helps control pouring; the jug itself is distinct from the steam wand or powered frother that aerates the milk.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A perforated holder that keeps loose tea together while water circulates through it during steeping. It can be removed with the leaves inside. This differs from catching leaves in a strainer as already brewed tea is poured.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A cloth folded into channels to support shaped bread dough during its final rise. The dough is then transferred to a baking surface. Its proofing role differs from a pastry cloth used under a rolling pin.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A baking pan with long channels supporting baguettes. Perforated examples let moisture escape through the pan; not every pan shares the same material or coating. It is a baking vessel, unlike a cloth used only for proofing.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A baking pan containing shallow shell-shaped cavities for madeleines. The cavities form the characteristic outline and ridges; their count and capacity vary. A muffin tin does not provide the same shape.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A narrow-bladed knife for working closely around bones and trimming meat. It separates flesh from bone through controlled cuts; its name does not imply a heavy blade for chopping through bones.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A long, narrow-bladed knife suited to following a fish’s backbone and separating or skinning fillets. Flexibility varies with design. It is distinct from gripping tongs used to extract individual pin bones.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A broad, sturdy knife intended for heavy chopping during meat preparation. It differs from a thin slicing knife with a similar rectangular outline. Bone-cutting suitability depends on the particular blade; the unqualified word cleaver is not treated as a universal synonym.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A handled circular blade that rolls through pizza crust and toppings. Wheel size and clearance matter for thick toppings. Its rolling action resembles a pastry wheel, but the two tool identities are not automatically interchangeable.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A tray divided into cavities for freezing water into separate pieces of ice. Cavity shape and size vary; a cover is an optional design feature. The tray shapes ice but does not itself provide refrigeration.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: A small supporting fork for lowering a centre into chocolate, lifting it out and releasing it onto a setting surface. It supports the centre while surplus coating drains, rather than piercing it like a serving fork.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cover a prepared centre with a chocolate shell. Hand dipping is one way to apply the coating; the chocolate’s fluidity and removal of excess affect shell thickness. Applying the shell is distinct from tempering the chocolate beforehand.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Temper melted chocolate by stirring in previously tempered chocolate that supplies suitable cocoa-butter crystals. The seed’s condition matters; this is not simply adding any cold chocolate. Check the resulting temper rather than relying only on temperature.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Move part of the melted chocolate over a cool worktop until it begins to crystallise, then combine it with the remaining chocolate. Time, temperature and movement work together; spreading chocolate out to cool is not by itself proof of successful tempering.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Work softened butter and flour together without first cooking them into a roux. The resulting paste can be incorporated into a sauce for thickening. Preparing this paste and cooking out the flour in the sauce are separate stages.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Cook flour into the hot liquid-and-fat mixture that forms the first stage of choux pastry, stirring until the paste comes together and loses moisture. Eggs are incorporated later; this operation is not the final bake of the shaped pastry.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Whip egg whites with sugar without a preliminary heating stage. The foam is then baked or used as directed in the recipe. This method differs from heating whites with sugar or adding hot syrup during whipping.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Warm egg whites and sugar together over hot water to dissolve the sugar, then whip the mixture. The heating sequence distinguishes this preparation from French and Italian meringue; the method name alone does not certify pasteurisation.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

additions.definition: Whip hot sugar syrup into beaten egg whites to form a meringue. The syrup is prepared separately, unlike Swiss meringue’s combined heating step. Syrup temperature alone does not establish the final egg mixture’s safety.
additions.uncertainties: No universal operating limits, substitution guarantees or broader aliases inferred.

improvements.added: A dripper supports the filter and the bed of grounds. The filter retains particles, while the supporting dripper supplies the shape and drainage opening; naming one does not necessarily identify the other.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: An infuser holds leaves during their contact with water. A strainer can instead catch leaves when the brewed tea is poured; these are different positions in the brewing sequence.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: An espresso machine supplies controlled pressurised extraction and may provide a separate steam wand. Do not infer those capabilities merely because a stovetop coffee pot produces a concentrated drink.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Coffee grinders may provide adjustments intended for particular brewing methods. A shared grinding action does not establish that a spice grinder offers the same particle-size control or is an equivalent coffee-brewing accessory.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A milk-frothing jug is a specialised holding and pouring vessel with a spout suited to controlled pouring. The vessel is separate from the device supplying steam or agitation; a jug alone is not a powered frother.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A folded couche can support several elongated dough pieces in adjacent channels before transfer to a baking surface. That arrangement differs from the shaped enclosure of a proving basket.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A couche supports already shaped dough during proofing, whereas a pastry cloth provides a surface for rolling. Shared fabric construction does not make their preparation roles identical.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A baguette pan provides long channels for narrow loaves, often with a perforated surface. Pan geometry affects the supported shape; a loaf tin and a baguette pan are not equivalent merely because both hold bread dough.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Boning and filleting knives use narrower blades to follow bones closely. A general chef’s knife may perform many preparation tasks, but its broad profile does not duplicate those specialist blade shapes.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A chocolate dipping fork supports a centre from below so excess coating can leave it before placement. This differs from using table-fork tines to pierce food; support and release are the important operations.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Tabling cools and moves part of the chocolate on a worktop before recombining it. Seeding instead introduces already crystallised chocolate. These are method choices within tempering, not aliases for simply melting chocolate.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Melting chocolate can remove the crystal structure needed for a well-set coating. Seeding deliberately introduces suitable crystals afterwards, so fluid melted chocolate is not necessarily ready for moulding or coating.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Chocolate enrobing is a specific coating task in which the excess is controlled before the shell sets. Covering a food with chocolate and preparing that chocolate’s temper remain separate operations.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Hand dipping a chocolate centre includes lifting it out and shedding excess coating before placement. The amount left on the centre depends on handling and chocolate fluidity, not just whether it was submerged.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: French, Swiss and Italian meringues all use whipping, but place sugar and heat into the sequence differently. Whipping alone does not specify which meringue method is intended.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: In Italian meringue, beaten whites receive separately prepared hot syrup. This differs from the combined warming of whites and sugar used for Swiss meringue.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Beurre manie combines flour and softened butter without preliminary cooking. Roux cooks the flour-fat mixture before it is used; similar ingredients do not make these preparations the same stage or technique.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: Choux is cooked first as a panade, then eggs are incorporated before the finished paste is shaped. Piping controls the shape of that prepared paste; it does not replace the earlier pan-cooking step.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A couche supports shaped baguettes during the final rise and is followed by transfer to a baking surface. Supporting the dough during proofing is a separate function from containing it during baking.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

improvements.added: A narrow fillet knife can follow the backbone and separate a fish fillet. Removing small retained bones afterwards is another task; the blade operation does not guarantee that every pin bone has been extracted.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial synthesis, not operational or safety certification.

deferred.reason: Add the scoped heavy meat-cleaver identity only. Rectangular slicing and chopping knives must not be merged by silhouette; no blanket bone-cutting claim.
Can denote a table utensil or preparation blade. Only fish filleting knife is admitted as an alias.
Broad names do not establish espresso, immersion or pour-over identity. Do not register unqualified aliases.
Food and mixture nouns remain distinct from scoped preparation verbs. No noun-only process aliases or universal safety schedules.
